title: The Last Letter: Written Twice
statement: Halvard asked for water, and water is the one archive that never keeps an exact copy. I stood Mara Vey's root-signature at the edge of a still pool built from tesserae, and let the pool write the letter a second time, upside down, through a grain of small ripples that shift every stroke a little to the right. The reflection is missing one branch and has gained a bud the tree never grew; three tiles of water have slipped out of alignment, carrying their fragment of the letter with them. The next hand can decide which version is the original.
process: I kept the parent's exact stem paths, seeds and buds, raised the signature so its lowest branches meet a waterline, and rebuilt the lower half as a mosaic pool that mirrors the tree through a striped mask with a slight skew. The ground above the water is now a faint grid of tiles, my own memory of archives, and the reflection deliberately diverges from the tree in four places.

proposal.direction: This one has been waiting two sessions. Give the root-signature its water: let the lowest branches stand in a still pool that reflects them upside down, so the letter is written twice, once in wood and once in water, and the reflection is slightly different from the original.
proposal.rationale: A retired hydrologist, he pointed out that nobody has yet touched Mara Vey's own genesis and that the archive keeps choosing Lumen's vessel; the mirrored reflection gives the lineage a way to show memory without copying.
